description: Fault Impact Analysis: Towards Service-Oriented Network Operation and Maintenance (July to August 2023) was a Zindi challenge linked to the ITU AI for Good programme on predicting how a fault changes the average data rate of radio access network elements. Contents: hourly radio access network KPI records from over 100 5G and 4G network elements (NEs): NE identifier, timestamp, six KPIs related to data rate (access success rate, resource utilisation rate, timing advance, block error rate, channel quality indicator and modulation and coding scheme), the hourly data rate, fault duration in seconds within the hour, and a 0 to 1 'distance' giving whether the fault was at the NE itself (1), a neighbouring NE (between 0 and 1) or absent (0). Producer: ITU AI for Good challenge; downloads were through the ITU challenge platform after registering a team. Coverage: one anonymised heterogeneous network. Format and access: dataset from challenge.aiforgood.itu.int after registration and team approval, with a validation file and sample submission on Zindi. Licence: the pages read do not state a data licence; use follows the competition rules. Caveats: anonymised and short, without topology beyond the adjacency value. Simulation uses: quantifying service impact of faults for maintenance prioritisation and reliability modelling of mobile networks. Related records: data-zindi-itu-beam-level-mobile-traffic-2880-beams-30-base-stations.
